verses.1: Therefore, I, the co-surgeon and witness to the sufferings of Christ, beg you to grant this request. I also desire to be part of the glory that will be revealed in the future.
verses.2: Obey the commands of God that are given to you. Do so willingly, not reluctantly or under pressure. Also, do it with joy and enthusiasm, not with resentment or anger.
verses.3: Nor as rulers over the flocks, but as leaders who guide them.
verses.4: And when the archbishop was revealed, he removed the crown of sin from that person who was considered worthy of glory.
verses.5: Similarly, the younger ones also served as underlings to the elders. All of them shared a sense of humility with each other, knowing that God opposes the proud and gives grace to those who are humble.
verses.6: They were humbled by the sovereign hand of God, so that He might raise you up at the right time.
verses.7: They took all of your worries upon themselves, so that they could take care of you.
verses.8: Hurry up, act quickly. Your judge is like the devil itself, constantly searching for someone to devour.
verses.9: You must stand firm in your faith, knowing that those same sufferings will also happen to your brothers in this world.
verses.10: But the God of all grace, who has called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will also strengthen, build up, care for, and support you, even though you may suffer a little bit.
verses.11: To him, the kingdom will last forever. Amen.
verses.12: For Siluanus, your faithful brother, I have written this in few words. I beg and urge you to believe that this is truly the will of God. Do as he desires.
verses.13: The assembly in Babylon and my son Márkos are claiming your rights.
verses.14: May you take pleasure in each other in love. May peace be upon you all who are in Christ.
